# Purpose

`sales_summary.R` generates a synthetic retail sales dataset, summarizes total revenue by region, and exports the results as a CSV file and a bar chart. It uses synthetic data only, so no real or personal data is involved.

# Inputs

The script reads no external files. It builds its own data from the parameters below.

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Rows (`n`) | 500 |
| Random seed | `set.seed(123)` |
| Regions | North, South, East, West |
| Categories | Electronics, Clothing, Home & Garden, Groceries |
| Dates | Random days in 2025 |
| Units per sale | Whole numbers from 1 to 20 |
| Unit price | Uniform between 5 and 120, rounded to 2 decimals |

## Required packages

- `dplyr` 1.0.0 or later (the script uses `summarise(.groups = ...)`)
- `ggplot2` (this also installs `scales`, which formats the chart axis)

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("dplyr", "ggplot2"))
```

# Outputs

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `output/revenue_by_region.csv` | Total revenue per region, sorted descending, rounded to 2 decimals |
| `output/revenue_by_region.png` | Bar chart of total revenue by region |

The script also prints the summary table to the console and ends with `All checks passed.` if every verification check succeeds.

# How the script works

The script has six numbered sections. Each snippet below is shown for explanation only and is not re-run here.

## 1. Setup

Load the packages, fix the random seed so results are reproducible, and create the output folder.

```{r setup-code, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(123)

dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 2. Generate synthetic data

Build a 500-row data frame by sampling each column, then add a `revenue` column (`units * unit_price`).

```{r data-code, eval=FALSE}
df <- data.frame(
  date       = sample(seq(as.Date("2025-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-31"), by = "day"),
                      n, replace = TRUE),
  region     = sample(regions, n, replace = TRUE),
  category   = sample(categories, n, replace = TRUE),
  units      = sample(1:20, n, replace = TRUE),
  unit_price = round(runif(n, min = 5, max = 120), 2)
) %>%
  mutate(revenue = units * unit_price)
```

## 3. Summarize

Group by region, total the revenue, round to 2 decimals, and sort from highest to lowest.

```{r summarize-code, eval=FALSE}
revenue_by_region <- df %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(total_revenue = round(sum(revenue), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_revenue))
```

## 4. Export

Write the summary table to CSV without row names.

```{r export-code, eval=FALSE}
write.csv(revenue_by_region, "output/revenue_by_region.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## 5. Visualize

Draw a bar chart ordered by revenue, format the y-axis with commas, and save it as a PNG.

```{r plot-code, eval=FALSE}
p <- ggplot(revenue_by_region,
            aes(x = reorder(region, -total_revenue), y = total_revenue)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "Total Revenue by Region", x = "Region", y = "Total Revenue") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("output/revenue_by_region.png", plot = p,
       width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

## 6. Verification checks

The script stops with an error if any check fails.

1. The data frame has exactly 500 rows.
2. Each region's total is recomputed in base R and compared with the summary table.
3. Both output files exist.

```{r checks-code, eval=FALSE}
stopifnot(nrow(df) == 500)

for (r in regions) {
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    round(sum(df$revenue[df$region == r]), 2),
    revenue_by_region$total_revenue[revenue_by_region$region == r]
  )))
}

stopifnot(file.exists("output/revenue_by_region.csv"),
          file.exists("output/revenue_by_region.png"))
```

# Example run

This section runs the full script. Knit this file from the same folder as `sales_summary.R` so the relative paths work.

```{r run-script}
source("sales_summary.R")
```

## Result table

```{r result-table}
knitr::kable(
  revenue_by_region,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Total revenue by region (synthetic data)"
)
```

## Result chart

```{r result-chart, out.width="80%", fig.alt="Bar chart of total revenue by region, sorted from highest to lowest"}
knitr::include_graphics("output/revenue_by_region.png")
```

# Reproducibility

Because the script uses `set.seed(123)`, repeated runs produce the same data and the same CSV. To confirm, run the script twice and compare the checksums:

```{r md5, eval=FALSE}
tools::md5sum("output/revenue_by_region.csv")
```
